source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Equation (2.1) is Euclidean Lipschitz continuity of tau; (2.2) is the tight bounded optimization; equation (2.3) explicitly weakens this to the first coordinate at equal second coordinate. The paper says known F is a 'leap of faith' and only notes that separate arm-mean Lipschitz restrictions would be a similar alternative.

The paper studies pre- and post-aggregation from unit-level boundary observations, defines aggregated boundary effects, and gives a convergence-rate/MSE theorem and asymptotic-normality theorem for pre-aggregation.

The source assumes i.i.d. unit-level observations, a continuous score density on compact support, differentiable arm mean functions, and a finite piecewise-linear boundary; it develops pointwise and uniform BATEC inference.
The paper formulates OT through generalized moments, proves convergence as hierarchy order increases, and discusses approximate linear quantities and support estimation from moments.

Moon partially identifies linear combinations of conditional mean outcomes from aggregate data using an optimization program, permits polyhedral restrictions, and gives plug-in bounds and valid conservative inference.
